articles.body: How Exposed Is VeloCloud Orchestrator? Reading ZoomEye Evidence Honestly When a vendor confirms active exploitation of a management-plane vulnerability, the first question from leadership is usually "how many of these do we have on the internet?" For CVE-2026-114625 in Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator, external search data can inform that answer, but only if the limits of the data are stated as clearly as the number. What was queried On 22 October 2026 a ZoomEye device query for the product title fingerprint, title="VeloCloud" , returned 520 matching assets. The query was executed against IPv4 device data and the stored count reflects the engine's total at that time. What the number means It counts hosts that advertise a VeloCloud-related page title. That is a product-family signal.

articles.title: Private Image Storage: Signed Download Links, Retention, and Object-Store Trade-offs
articles.excerpt: Short answer: keep the bucket private, put a short-lived signed URL behind an authorization check, and enforce deletion with a lifecycle worker that records every decision. The cheapest design is the…
articles.body: Short answer: keep the bucket private, put a short-lived signed URL behind an authorization check, and enforce deletion with a lifecycle worker that records every decision. The cheapest design is the one that deletes the right bytes on time; a low storage rate does not rescue a retention process that cannot prove what it removed. In a property-management AI app, generated images are easy to create and surprisingly hard to retire. A signed lease scan, inspection photo, or model-generated renovation mockup may have a contractual deletion deadline. The bill is made of stored bytes, request operations, and delivery traffic. For most small systems, retention duration and egress dominate the conversation long before metadata does.

articles.title: Parsing Property Owner Names in pandas: Individuals, Joint Owners, Trusts and LLCs
articles.excerpt: If you have pulled a parcel list from a county assessor or recorder, you have seen the owner name field. It looks like a name column, but it holds far more: two spouses in one cell, a trust with a tru…
articles.body: If you have pulled a parcel list from a county assessor or recorder, you have seen the owner name field. It looks like a name column, but it holds far more: two spouses in one cell, a trust with a trustee tucked in, a business entity, a deceased owner's estate, plus Latin abbreviations that mean "and others." Before you send a list out for skip tracing, you need to know who (or what) each record actually is. A skip trace on SMITH JOHN & MARY ETUX as one literal string won't work well. Sending MAIN STREET HOLDINGS LLC through a person search is a waste.

articles.title: Part 5: After the Dispatch - Handling Delivery Events
articles.excerpt: Part 4 ended on one word in the Communications logs: [Email:Simulation.Email:Dispatched] ... [Sms:Simulation.Sms:Dispatched] ... [Push:Simulation.Push:Dispatched] ... Dispatched means a provider accep…
articles.body: Part 4 ended on one word in the Communications logs: [Email:Simulation.Email:Dispatched] ... [Sms:Simulation.Sms:Dispatched] ... [Push:Simulation.Push:Dispatched] ... Dispatched means a provider accepted the message. It doesn't mean anyone received it. With the simulator the two happen together. With a real provider they don't. Twilio accepts an SMS and returns a message id straight away, then reports back as the message moves along: queued, sent, delivered, or undelivered because the handset was unreachable. Email providers report bounces and opens. Push services report invalid tokens. Those updates are worth keeping. Support wants to know whether the customer really got the order confirmation. Engineering wants to know which provider is failing.

articles.title: If I can't patch it the same day, I don't host it myself
articles.excerpt: Two critical PHP bugs came out this week. Both can let an attacker run code on a server. No login needed. Today I got an email from Hetzner. The message was simple: you run your own server, so the upd…
articles.body: Two critical PHP bugs came out this week. Both can let an attacker run code on a server. No login needed. Today I got an email from Hetzner. The message was simple: you run your own server, so the update is your job. So I checked my own setup. My sites run WordPress on managed hosting. The host patched PHP for me. I only checked the build date. My Hetzner server has no PHP on it. Nothing to patch this time. The funny part: a few days earlier I was thinking about moving my WordPress sites to that server. It would save some money. This week showed me the real cost. On my own server, the patch is my job. The same day. Maybe at night. And that server runs my automation. A hacked WordPress next to it is a risk for everything else. So the sites stay on managed hosting for now.

articles.title: Europe's Space Rider vehicle comes crashing down during drop test
articles.excerpt: The full-scale prototype of Europe's Space Rider orbiter failed to deploy its parachute during a drop test earlier this month, but ESA officials hope the setback won't delay progress toward its first…
articles.body: Europe has dropped the ball on the prototype for its first reusable spacecraft. Or, rather, the prototype itself was dropped — on purpose — but the outcome of its fall was not what engineers had hoped for. The incident occurred during an Oct. 6 drop test of the full-scale Space Rider model , from the European Space Agency (ESA). The robotic vehicle's initial drogue parachute deployed successfully, but its main parafoil detached during deployment, leaving the prototype unable to slow its descent before crashing into the ground, according to ESA officials. The cause of the failure remains under investigation.

articles.body: NASA, ESA, Michael Jones (California Institute of Technology); Image Processing: Gladys Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America) This NASA Hubble Space Telescope image released on Oct. 16, 2026, features the edge-on, intermediate spiral galaxy NGC 1827, located roughly 37 million light-years away in the constellation Columba, the Dove. Hubble captured the image as part of a survey looking at 260 satellite galaxies around 22 Milky Way-like host galaxies within a radius of about 32 million light-years from Earth. Low-mass galaxies like the ones in this Hubble observing program provide a way to test the predictions of cosmological models on small scales, which struggle to match observations.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 22, 1992: Ashes of 'Star Trek' creator Gene Roddenberry launch into space on NASA shuttle
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 22, 1992, the space shuttle Columbia launched into space with the ashes of Gene Roddenberry, the creator of "Star Trek." Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 22, 1992, the space shuttle Columbia launched into space with the ashes of Gene Roddenberry, the creator of " Star Trek ," aboard. During mission STS-52, NASA astronaut and shuttle commander James Wetherbee brought a small container with a portion of Roddenberry's ashes into space as part of his personal effects at the request of Roddenberry's widow, Majel Barrett . It was Roddenberry's lifelong dream to go to space, but he never got to go while he was alive. But thanks to his wife, a little bit of Roddenberry finally made it to space almost exactly one year after his death. NASA and his family didn't tell anyone about it until almost two years later in 1994. Wetherbee said he was "honored to be asked" by Barrett to carry Roddenberry's ashses on the spaceflight.

articles.body: Meta has re-enabled Muse sharing after security researchers had reported that public conversation links could be easy to find. The researchers said they had been able to find Muse pages like a marketing company's internal revenue review and a small business owner's loan application. Researchers at Claroc reported earlier this week that Muse the web addresses for shared conversations from Muse were named after a conversation's title and written into public DNS. Ars Technica said Tuesday that Meta paused the sharing feature after it reached out about what was going on. articles.title: The 2027 total solar eclipse will plunge these 10 ancient Egyptian temples and monuments into darkness
articles.excerpt: The "eclipse of the century" will plunge some of ancient Egypt's most spectacular sites into darkness on Aug. 2, 2027. These temples, tombs and monuments are inside the path of totality.
articles.body: The total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027, has an ancient feel. It will certainly be a celestial event for the ages — at 6 minutes 23 seconds, it will feature the longest totality on land of the 21st century and the longest anywhere until 2114. However, its point of greatest eclipse occurs just a few miles from Thebes, the magnificent religious and political capital of ancient Egypt's Middle Kingdom and New Kingdom. On the east bank of the mighty Nile is Luxor, the great city of the living, with its massive temple complexes of Karnak and Luxor. On its west bank is the city of the dead, which includes the Valley of the Kings and the Temple of Hatshepsut. Modern Luxor, population 285,000, is set to become a focal point for eclipse chasers on Aug.

articles.title: Tesla now says it needs its own maps for FSD after years of dismissing maps
articles.excerpt: Tesla says it’s building its own maps to fix some of the most common problems with its “Full Self-Driving” system, including reading speed limits, parking, and choosing routes. The company’s head of A…
articles.body: Tesla says it’s building its own maps to fix some of the most common problems with its “Full Self-Driving” system, including reading speed limits, parking, and choosing routes. The company’s head of AI described the effort on Tesla’s Q3 2026 earnings call. It’s a notable shift for a company whose CEO spent years arguing that self-driving systems relying on maps are brittle. And it shows Tesla’s fleet is now doing the same job Waymo’s cars do: mapping the roads so the self-driving system knows what it can’t reliably figure out on its own.
